upset_of_the_week.basis: recorded when the week's picks were made: up to 3 underdogs the model rates at least 5 points above the market, biggest gap first, in FBS games involving at least one Power Four team, excluding teams outplayed on EPA in their most recent game
upset_of_the_week.caveat: Editorial, not advice. This is the model's most contrarian call of the week, and disagreement of this kind has historically predicted WORSE results on our graded college samples, not better. Publish it as something to watch and grade afterwards, never as a recommended bet.

scorecard.caveat: A hit rate alone overstates this. The cards are mostly heavy favourites, so the model expects to win nearly all of them: read hit_rate_pct next to expected_hit_rate_pct, and read beat_market_pct, which has been below 50%. Never render the hit rate on its own.

scope.winner_note: Every record on this page is straight-up: did the team the model favoured win the game. That is what it is built to answer.
scope.spread_note: It is not a spread record. Against the closing line the model has not beaten break-even, and margin is a different question from outcome -- it cannot see a coach empty the bench at 42-0.
scope.conviction_note: Where it earns its keep is disagreement: on close games it prices the underdog several points higher than the market does. That is a read on who is underrated, not a claim to beat the price.
